newsitem.title: ITALY: IBCA puts BancoNapoli, BNL on credit watch.
newsitem.headline: IBCA puts BancoNapoli, BNL on credit watch.

text.p: European credit rating agency IBCA said it placed the short-term, long-term and individual ratings of Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) on a rating watch with negative implications.

In a statement received in Milan, IBCA also said it placed the short-term, long-term and individual ratings of Banco di Napoli on rating watch with positive implications. BNL's short-term rating is now A1, long-term is A+ and individual C/D. Banco Napoli's short-term rating is currently A3, long-term BBB and individual E.
Both banks' legal rating of two are unchanged.

IBCA referred to a successful bid by BNL and insurer INA for a 60 percent stake in Banco di Napoli and said a new management team reorganising Banco Napoli had set down new procedures and systems and provided substantially against impaired loans.

The setting up of a "bad bank" into which problem loans would be transferred before the sale was completed would limit further provisioning requirements and the bank had had an injection of capital from the Italian Treasury.
"However, at least initially the costs involved with the acquisition may have a negative impact on BNL's profitability and on its solvency," IBCA said.
"At end-1995, BNL which is 85 percent held by the Italian Treasury had equity of 7,141 billion lire and a total capital ratio of 9.66 percent. It is as yet unclear how it will pay for its purchase."
